statement: The spouse and children of an entrepreneur parolee may be paroled as derivatives, each filing Form I-131 with evidence of the qualifying relationship and for no longer than the entrepreneur's parole period; the spouse, after being paroled into the United States, may be eligible for employment authorization and requests it on Form I-765 under 8 CFR 274a.13, while a child of the entrepreneur parolee may not be authorized for and may not accept employment (8 CFR § 212.19(h)(1)-(4)).
caveat: Derivative parole and the spouse's employment authorization are separate discretionary, case-by-case grants with their own applications and fees, and the spouse may not work until the employment authorization is granted. Immigration decisions need counsel.
reviewer: Lane editorial review (immigration deep dive 2026-10-19); independent domain expert review pending
